title: MSP-MVS Multi-granularity Segmentation Prior Guided Multi-View Stereo

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction / 'In summary, our contributions are as follows' vs Abstract
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Abstract and Conclusion describe MSP-MVS's contributions as (1) multi-granularity segmentation prior via Semantic-SAM, (2) anchor equidistribution, and (3) iterative local search optimization. However, the Introduction's explicit 'contributions' list states entirely different items: '1) We propose a novel joint hypothesis filter...2) We present an iterative correlation refinement procedure...3) We introduce a textureless-aware segmentation technique...'. These describe a completely different method (matching the separately cited 'TSAR-MVS' paper) and directly contradict the method actually described and ablated later in the paper (segmentation prior, anchor equidistribution, ILS), which never appear in this contributions list.

predicted_errors.error_location: Mid-paper paragraph: 'Therefore, we propose TSAR-MVS, a generalized post-processing MVS method...'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper is titled 'MSP-MVS' and its abstract/conclusion describe a PatchMatch patch-deformation method guided by multi-granularity segmentation. Yet the body text explicitly states 'we propose TSAR-MVS, a generalized post-processing MVS method that sequentially applies confidence-based outliers filtering, superpixel-based local refinement, and feature-based area generation...' — introducing a different named method with an entirely different mechanism (post-processing filter vs. PatchMatch patch deformation), which is incompatible with the rest of the paper's described architecture.

predicted_errors.error_location: Related Work: 'TAPA-MVS..., PCF-MVS..., and TSAR-MVS (Yuan et al. 2024b) attempt to employ superpixel planarization...' vs earlier text introducing 'TSAR-MVS' as 'our method'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Earlier in the paper, TSAR-MVS is presented as the authors' own proposed method ('we propose TSAR-MVS...'), while later in the Related Work section TSAR-MVS (Yuan et al. 2024b) is cited as a pre-existing third-party method alongside TAPA-MVS and PCF-MVS that 'severely affected by limited superpixel size' — a weakness being critiqued. This is self-contradictory: the same name cannot simultaneously be the paper's own novel contribution and a flawed prior work being criticized.

predicted_errors.error_location: 'Experiments on extensive datasets, including the ETH3D high-resolution dataset, Tanks & Temples dataset and Strecha dataset demonstrate...' vs Experimental section: 'We evaluate our work on ETH3D benchmark...and Tanks & Temples benchmark (TNT)...'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims evaluation on three datasets (ETH3D, TNT, and Strecha), but the actual Experiments section only describes evaluation on ETH3D and TNT, with no mention or results reported for the Strecha dataset anywhere in the described quantitative/qualitative results.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract: 'The state-of-the-art results on ETH3D and Tanks & Temples benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and robust generalization ability of our proposed method.'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Experiments section itself admits: 'our method achieves the second best results in the TNT advanced datasets, falling short by less than 0.3% in F1 score compared to EPNet'. This contradicts the blanket claim of achieving 'state-of-the-art results...on Tanks & Temples benchmarks', since the method is not state-of-the-art on the TNT Advanced subset.

predicted_errors.error_location: Paragraph beginning 'Specifically, we first introduce a joint hypothesis filter...' through 'another WMF is adopted to interpolate the depths and normals of the remaining pixels.'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: This section describes a pipeline based on confidence estimation, disparity discontinuity detection, RANSAC superpixel planarization, and weighted median filtering as a post-processing refinement of existing depth maps. This is methodologically incompatible with the PatchMatch-based patch deformation, anchor equidistribution, and iterative local search optimization framework that is described as MSP-MVS's actual mechanism in the Abstract, Related Work (Semantic-SAM discussion), and Ablation Study sections — the two described methods cannot coexist as a single consistent architecture.
